tagline.text: A vast communal pasture facing the Pacific in southern Batan

location.label: Location
location.text: Communal pasture in Mahatao, southern Batan Island

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: March–June, clear days after 10 a.m. or at sunset

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱50–500 (registration fee and a one-way tricycle ride from Basco)

children.text: Racuh a Payaman means "wide pasture" in Ivatan, and it is a communal pasture spreading over the seaside of Mahatao in southern Batan Island. Surf-battered cliffs, herds of cattle and carabao, and views of Tayid Lighthouse and Mount Iraya in the distance are why it is commonly called Marlboro Country.

Racuh a Payaman is a wide communal pasture stretching along the eastern coast of southern Batan Island. In Ivatan, "racuh" means wide and "payaman" refers to a pasture, so the name literally means a wide pasture. Among travelers it is better known by the nicknames Marlboro Country and Marlboro Hills, because the scenery looks like something from a cigarette advertisement. Most sources place it in Mahatao, while some older blogs put it in Uyugan or Imnajbu, which causes some confusion. Locally, directions are given from the Mahatao side entrance.

What makes this place special is the scale of the landscape. Nearly treeless green hills roll gently and then suddenly drop toward the sea, where big Pacific waves pound the cliffs below. Cattle, carabao and horses graze across the hills or rest in shallow hollows in the grass, and the animals are known to be raised jointly by members of the Mahatao communal pasture association. Because this is working ranchland with owners, the basic etiquette is not to approach, touch or try to ride the animals. When taking photos, avoid loud noises that might startle them, and do not leave your belongings unattended on the grass.

The views from the hilltop are well worth the walk. On one side you can see Tayid Lighthouse on its hill across the water, on the other Mount Iraya, the central peak of Batan Island, and in between, below, the green cliffs and waves of Diura Beach. Some visitors report that on clear days you can even see a small island floating in the sea to the north. That is why many people say this is the stop where they spend the longest taking photos on the South Batan day tour. Knowing a little about pasture culture on Batan makes the view look different. Batan is a windy island, and this pasture is a communal grazing ground shared by the villagers. It is not a theme park that sells tickets but land where animals are still at work, so keep that in mind. The distance from Naidi Hills, home of Basco Lighthouse, to Mahatao town is described as about
15 km
, and Diura fishing village is about
3 km
from Mahatao town proper, so you can link the sights easily along one road.

Getting here is simple. Most people hire a tricycle from Basco Airport or town and stop here as one part of the South Batan tour, and sources describe paying a small registration fee at the registration office on the Mahatao town side. From the entrance to the good viewpoints on the hills you must climb along narrow paths and grass, so comfortable shoes are a must. The prices and rules in this guide include reviews from several years ago, so please check the latest information at the local tourism office before you go. For first-time visitors we suggest the following: leave Basco early in the morning, see Chawa Viewdeck and Tayid Lighthouse, and arrive at the pasture around

a.m. to stay for more than an hour. Some reviews say this is the place where they stayed longest on the whole tour, and between taking photos and walking, time passes quickly. Rushing through at midday, on the other hand, makes it hard to feel the scale of the landscape. Weather on Batan can change several times a day, so it also helps to be patient and wait a little for the clouds to clear.

The heart of the scene is gentle, nearly treeless hills that run toward the sea and end abruptly in cliffs. With sea and grass in one frame, people often compare it to New Zealand or the Shire from The Lord of the Rings.

Cattle, carabao and horses roam the grass with no fences. You often see them resting in shallow hollows, and putting an animal in the foreground of a photo brings the scene to life. Just keep your distance from them.
From the hilltop you can see Tayid Lighthouse on one side and Mount Iraya on the other, with Diura Beach below in between. Look for a spot that lets you capture all three in a single shot.

The end of the green hills is a cliff that takes the full force of the Pacific waves. You can see a rocky islet rising from the middle of the surf. The cliff edge is steep and windy, so do not go right up to it.

blocks.title: Light that changes through the day

children.text: Early in the morning the hills carry long shadows, and after
a.m. the sunlight falls straight down and the green is at its most vivid. Many reviews say sunset is lovely too, but you must arrange your ride back in advance.

blocks.title: Narrow walking paths across the grass

children.text: Several narrow footpaths run between the hills so you can walk to different viewpoints. Getting from the entrance to the main viewpoint takes quite a bit of time and energy. Many travelers stay in one spot for a long time.
Sources mention a restaurant and restrooms across the road. Honesty Coffee Shop is also nearby, a good place for coffee during the South Batan tour. Check opening hours locally.

items.title: A stop on the South Batan tour
items.subtitle: A loop of the south by tricycle from Basco

children.text: Hire a tricycle at Basco Airport or in town and start the South Batan tour. Chawa Viewdeck is usually the first stop.
First visit Tayid Lighthouse and San Carlos Borromeo Church in Mahatao. Sources say you register for the pasture at the registration office next to the church.

Arrive at Racuh a Payaman. The sunlight is coming straight down at this hour, so the hills look their greenest. Follow the path up to the viewpoint on the hill and feel free to stay for more than 1 hour.
Rest with lunch and coffee at a nearby restaurant or Honesty Coffee Shop.
Continue to Imnajbu Beach, the Alapad rock formations and the House of Dakay, then return to Basco.
The order differs a little from review to review. It is best to talk with your driver and allot the most time to the pasture.

items.title: Relaxed route
items.subtitle: Enjoying morning shadows and sunset light

children.text: Leave Basco early. In the early morning the hills carry long shadows, which gives photos a different mood.
Walk the pasture hills and watch the cattle and carabao. The wind is strong, so fasten your hat firmly.
Move on to other stops in the south. Arrange your ride back with the driver in advance.
If you want to visit at sunset, check your ride back and the sunset time beforehand.
Travel from Manila to Basco (BSO) by air. Routes and frequencies change, so check with the airline.
Flights to Batanes are often canceled because of weather, so leave some slack in your schedule.
Flights to Batanes depend heavily on the weather. Check the latest flight notices.
Reviews say a tricycle from Basco Airport or town toward Honesty Coffee Shop takes about
30–40 minutes
(2014 and 2025 sources agree).
Hiring a tricycle for the whole South Batan tour is the most common approach. Reviews from 2014 and 2020 quote about
per tricycle, and some recent reviews mention about
for two people, but this could not be confirmed, so negotiate with the driver first.
For public transport, you can take a jeepney from Basco to Mahatao, get off at the municipal hall and switch to a tricycle, but it is hard to find a ride back.
Sources say you can go by rental car or motorbike yourself. Parking is said to be available near the entrance, so check locally.
The pasture looks very different by season. First decide whether you prefer the vivid green after rain or the cooler sea views on clear days.

During the day, many say the time after 10 a.m., when the sun shines straight down, is best for photos, and early morning and sunset also have a nice mood. The wind is strong, so bring a jacket in any season.

Most people stay in Basco town and visit here on a day trip of the South Batan tour. Choose between guesthouses in Basco town and Mahatao with travel time in mind. In peak season flights and rooms fill up early, so booking ahead is safer.

For meals you will use the restaurant across from the entrance or restaurants in Mahatao and Imnajbu during the South Batan tour. You can try Ivatan local food at restaurants in Basco town. The nearby Honesty Coffee Shop is known as an unstaffed shop, so check how it works on site.

It is better to decide what to drink and eat before you set out. Bring water and snacks from Basco, and lunch fits easily at a restaurant along the tour route. Restaurant hours and menus change often, so ask your driver.
On clear days after 10 a.m. the green of the hills is at its most vivid.
The wind is very strong, so fasten your hat, camera strap and drone securely.
The hills can be slippery, so wear firm sneakers or sandals.
It is a long walk from the entrance to the viewpoint, so bring water and sunscreen.
Getting a ride back is difficult, so ask your driver to wait or come on a tour.
Take all your trash with you. This is a communal pasture and a protected landscape.
Check the latest notices from the local authority or tour operator for drone rules.
At busy hours tripods line up at the popular viewpoints. Going early in the morning or late in the afternoon is quieter.
It is hard to find your group on a wide grassland if you get separated. Agree on a meeting spot and time in advance.
The cliff edge is steep and windy, so do not stand at the edge. The animals have owners, so keep your distance.
Do not touch or ride the cattle, carabao or horses.
Low grass covers the cliff edge, making it hard to see where you step.
Fees and registration rules differ from review to review and need to be confirmed locally.
The grass is slippery after rain.
During typhoon season flights and tours may be suspended, so check the latest notices.
Clouds or fog can roll in suddenly and block your view, so come down from the hill early if the weather turns bad.
